codeReview.summary: The shared wrapper refactor landed across all eight changed Convex HTTP route files and the public/internal helper deduplication remains intact, but the new error categorization is incomplete. `withErrorHandling` only preserves explicit `HttpError`s plus a small not-found/conflict phrase list, so many existing plain `Error("... is required")` validation failures now fall through to HTTP 500 instead of the 400-class responses the feature description and VAL-CNVX-004 require.

issues.description: `categorizeError()` only maps explicit `HttpError`s and a narrow set of 404/409 substrings before defaulting everything else to 500 at line 81. Several wrapped handlers still delegate input validation to downstream Convex mutations/helpers that throw plain errors such as `name is required`, `kind is required`, `userName is required`, and `status is required` (`convex/lists.ts:17,27`, `convex/messageTemplates.ts:8,23`, `convex/instagramAccounts.ts:23,62,134`). Because routes like `convex/httpRoutes/lists.ts:31`, `convex/httpRoutes/messageTemplates.ts:22`, and `convex/httpRoutes/instagramAccounts.ts:27,91` do not convert those failures to `ValidationError`, those validation requests now return 500 instead of 400, so the feature does not fully satisfy the promised validation-status categorization.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The `refactor-worker` skill says new functionality should get failing tests first, but this feature changed HTTP status semantics without adding any dedicated regression coverage and still recorded `followedProcedure: true`.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/skills/refactor-worker/SKILL.md:44-45` says to write failing tests first for new functionality. The handoff for session `3323b121-e841-4ce9-8387-c0205ffaee2f` records `tests.added: []` and `followedProcedure: true` (`C:/Users/yaros/.factory/missions/c159f8a2-f42a-48c7-bea6-166e5c18ca91/handoffs/2026-03-14T19-44-53-189Z__convex-error-handling__3323b121-e841-4ce9-8387-c0205ffaee2f.json:62,67`).

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared state does not currently document that many Convex domain helpers signal client-input problems via plain `Error` message strings rather than typed errors, so HTTP wrappers must preserve a central message-to-status mapping for validation/conflict phrases.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `.factory/library/architecture.md` lists Convex route counts and integration seams but does not mention this error-message convention. Existing helpers still throw plain validation/conflict strings in `convex/lists.ts:17,27`, `convex/messageTemplates.ts:8,23`, `convex/instagramAccounts.ts:23,62,134`, and `convex/workflows/helpers.ts:87`, while `convex/httpRoutes/shared.ts:47-81` now depends on string categorization to choose HTTP status codes.

summary: Reviewed `convex-error-handling` via the mission feature record, handoff, transcript skeleton, `refactor-worker` skill, validation contract, and `git show` for commit `6fb8fa469a2e35d988434c222f8ab9613728c448`. The wrapper rollout itself is comprehensive, but the new shared categorizer misses existing plain validation errors, causing some HTTP validation failures to regress to 500, so I marked the feature as failing and recorded skill/knowledge gaps that helped the regression slip through.
